name: The White Man's Burden
scope: The doctrine the defining sources tie to the phrase 'the white man's burden': Kipling's 1899 poem (subtitled 'The United States and the Philippine Islands') and the imperial argument they read in it, that Western, white-ruled nations have a moral duty to govern and 'civilise' peoples they judge less developed, at the cost of the rulers' own sacrifice and without thanks (Britannica; EBSCO Research Starter; GradeSaver; the Victorian Prose and Poetry edition). It takes the poem's text and the sources' account of it, including the American-expansion use (Theodore Roosevelt, the Philippines). It excludes the broader 'civilizing mission', manifest destiny, imperialism and white supremacy, which are separate entries, and the critics' replies (Twain, Labouchère, Morel, Arendt), which only show it is an ideology.
